Licensed RCICs (RCIC No. R711592) help individuals, families and employers compare and pursue Canadian permanent residence, temporary residence, work and study permits, family sponsorship, citizenship and complex refusal or appeal matters. Guidance is grounded in current IRCC and provincial requirements; no outcome is guaranteed.

topics.metaDescription: Free Canada immigration calculators and self-service tools — CRS score, PNP eligibility, NOC occupation finder and a document checklist.
topics.lead: A hub of free, no-obligation self-service tools for anyone planning a Canadian immigration application: a CRS calculator for Express Entry, a provincial nominee program eligibility check, a NOC occupation finder, and a document checklist. The tools give an indicative picture only; a licensed RCIC review is the reliable next step.

topics.label: CRS Calculator Canada
topics.seoTitle: CRS Calculator Canada | Free Express Entry Score Tool
topics.metaDescription: Estimate your Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) score for Express Entry in minutes with this free calculator, then check how to improve it.
topics.lead: The Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) is the points grid IRCC uses to rank Express Entry candidates. This free calculator estimates a score across core human capital (age, education, language, work experience), spouse or partner factors, skill transferability and additional points such as a provincial nomination or a job offer. It is indicative only — official scores are calculated by IRCC from your profile.

topics.label: PNP Eligibility Check Canada
topics.seoTitle: PNP Eligibility Check Canada | Free Provincial Nominee Tool
topics.metaDescription: Check which Provincial Nominee Programs may fit your profile — free eligibility check across Canada s provinces and territories.
topics.lead: Each Canadian province and territory runs its own Provincial Nominee Program (PNP) with its own streams, occupation lists and criteria. This free check gives an indicative read on which PNPs may be worth exploring based on your occupation, experience, language ability and ties to a province. A nomination can add significant points to an Express Entry profile and is one of the most direct routes to permanent residence for candidates outside the top of the federal pool.

topics.label: NOC / Occupation Finder Canada
topics.seoTitle: NOC / Occupation Finder Canada | Find Your NOC Code
topics.metaDescription: Find the National Occupational Classification (NOC) code and TEER category for your job — the first step in most Canadian immigration applications.
topics.lead: Canada s National Occupational Classification (NOC) assigns every occupation a code and a TEER category. Almost every economic immigration program — Express Entry, most PNPs, LMIA-based work permits — turns on which NOC code your job experience matches and whether it is TEER 0, 1, 2 or 3. This finder helps you locate the code and category that best fit your duties, which should then be confirmed against the official NOC description.
